scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO focuses on developing next-generation AI agent architectures powered by large language models (LLMs), capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and action execution to achieve specified goals based on high-level instructions.

MAESTRO develops a hybrid neuro-symbolic planning engine combining LLM-based reasoning with formal symbolic planning methods including Monte Carlo Tree Search, hierarchical task networks, self-correction through plan monitoring, and verifiable sub-task decomposition with pre/post-conditions and verification checkpoints.

MAESTRO designs a unified adaptive memory architecture integrating working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory managed by a memory controller, enabling effective long-horizon state management extending beyond the context window of any single LLM call.

MAESTRO develops decentralised multi-agent coordination protocols with formal task-delegation, conflict resolution mechanisms, convergence guarantees, and auditable interaction traces enabling heterogeneous agent collaboration on shared objectives.

MAESTRO develops an External Tool and API Orchestration Layer providing a typed tool registry with capability models, formal tool selection and invocation policies, standardised API adapters abstracting heterogeneous protocols (REST, GraphQL, HL7 FHIR, OPC-UA), post-invocation verification and grounding, execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, and auditable tool execution traces.

Validation through a healthcare clinical decision support demonstrator co-designed with clinical partners, integrating HL7 FHIR APIs and diagnostic knowledge bases, validated against real diagnostic pathways at TRL 5 with quantitative KPIs including diagnostic accuracy and tool invocation success rate benchmarked against clinician baselines.

Validation through an advanced manufacturing process optimisation multi-agent demonstrator using OPC-UA industrial connectors, digital twin APIs, and sensor data streams, validated in operational factory environments at TRL 5 with quantitative KPIs including defect rate reduction, energy savings, and coordination latency.

Validation through a logistics and supply chain cross-sector transfer demonstrator to confirm architecture portability beyond the three call-identified priority sectors, with the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer managing logistics tracking, customs clearance, and carrier scheduling APIs.

MAESTRO does not provide an in-vehicle autonomous driving full demonstrator; instead, WP8 provides a targeted architectural mapping analysis assessing transferability of the MAESTRO architecture to autonomous driving settings.
scope_findings.flag_reason: SR-11 identifies in-vehicle autonomous driving as a call-priority sector for portfolio coverage preferential treatment (status: Confirmed). The absence of a direct demonstrator in this sector and its replacement with a WP8 architectural mapping analysis is not constitutionally out-of-scope — CC-09 operates as a portfolio mechanism requiring at least one funded proposal per priority sector across the portfolio, and does not individually require each proposal to address all three sectors. However, no Tier 2B scope element defines 'architectural mapping analysis' as a recognised form of sector engagement for portfolio coverage purposes. The boundary between meaningful sector engagement and non-engagement within SR-11 and CC-09 is unresolved in scope_requirements.json. Evaluators applying the CC-09 portfolio coverage mechanism may assess whether the WP8 analysis constitutes sufficient focus on this sector to qualify for any portfolio benefit. Flagged for resolution in the proposal's impact and methodology sections.

scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO allocates dedicated tasks for cohesion activities with ADRA and the GenAI4EU central Hub (CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18).

All communicable research results — frameworks, models, benchmarks, the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, and demonstrator results — will be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
The project will link to the resources offered by AI Factories and Data Labs for compute-intensive training and evaluation.
Demonstrator results will be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities and disseminated via European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).
MAESTRO incorporates qualitative and quantitative KPIs, standardised benchmarking across all demonstrators, and structured progress monitoring at 6-month integration checkpoints.
MAESTRO directly serves and contributes to the Apply AI Strategy by advancing foundational capabilities for trustworthy AI deployment in key European economic sectors.
The project duration is 48 months.
scope_findings.flag_reason: CC-14 (max_project_duration_months) has status 'Assumed' in call_constraints.json — the 48-month maximum duration is not explicitly stated in the topic text and the constraint record notes that verification against Tier 1 General Annex B is required. The project duration claim of 48 months sits exactly at the assumed maximum limit. If the confirmed constraint from Tier 1 differs, the project duration may require adjustment. Flagged pending confirmation of the maximum duration from Tier 1 General Annex B per the CC-14 assumption note.

scope_findings.claim: The requested EU contribution is €18,500,000.

MAESTRO's open-source framework and standardised agent interaction protocols will lower barriers for European SMEs and startups to build on next-generation AI agent technology, strengthening the European AI ecosystem's competitiveness and reducing strategic dependency on non-European AI platforms.
scope_findings.flag_reason: No Tier 2B scope element found to confirm these claims as within the defined scope boundary. The closest scope elements are SR-05/CC-05 (sharing communicable results via the AI-on-demand platform) and CC-13 (contributing to the Apply AI Strategy), but the specific claims — 'lowering barriers for European SMEs and startups' and 'reducing strategic dependency on non-European AI platforms' — extend beyond the scope boundary defined in scope_requirements.json. Per the constitutional constraint that scope boundary is defined by Tier 2B only (CLAUDE.md §13.2), these claims cannot be confirmed as in-scope from the files consulted. They may be appropriate for the impact narrative and should be grounded against Tier 2B expected_impacts.json rather than the scope boundary sources consulted here.

scope_findings.claim: The MAESTRO architecture is asserted to be architecturally transferable to in-vehicle autonomous driving settings based on its real-time multi-agent coordination, verified planning under safety constraints, and tool/API integration including sensor APIs and V2X communication interfaces, assessed in a WP8 architectural mapping analysis.
scope_findings.flag_reason: SR-11 (status: Confirmed) identifies in-vehicle autonomous driving as a priority sector where proposals focusing on this sector may receive preferential treatment. The assertion of architectural transferability to this sector partially aligns with SR-11 by claiming thematic relevance, but the claim is based on an architectural mapping analysis (WP8) rather than demonstrated sector validation. SR-11 frames priority sector engagement in terms of proposals that 'focus on' the sector and 'pass all evaluation thresholds,' implying direct demonstrator-level engagement rather than analytical assertion of transferability. The claim is borderline: it partially overlaps with SR-11 (architectural relevance to the priority sector is asserted) while the form of engagement may be insufficient to satisfy portfolio coverage intent under CC-09. Flagged because the scope boundary entry SR-11 is Confirmed but the claim's engagement modality creates interpretive ambiguity that requires resolution before proposal submission.

scope_findings.claim: The strategic positioning document references 'SR-04' as the essential requirement that integration of external tools and APIs is necessary to overcome limitations of large AI models and enhance agent performance; however, in scope_requirements.json SR-04 defines the ADRA/GenAI4EU cohesion activities requirement. The external tools and APIs requirement corresponds to SR-02(c) in scope_requirements.json.
scope_findings.flag_reason: Internal numbering inconsistency in the project brief: strategic_positioning.md uses the label 'SR-04' to reference the external tools and APIs requirement, which corresponds to SR-02(c) in scope_requirements.json. SR-04 in scope_requirements.json defines the ADRA/GenAI4EU cohesion activities requirement. The project concept addresses both requirements substantively, so this is a document labelling error rather than a scope gap. However, if proposal text carries this mislabelling, it risks evaluator confusion when cross-referencing call requirements. Flagged for correction in the concept note and strategic positioning documents before these feed into proposal section drafts.
